declarations.docstring: Inductive predicate identifying finite-length objects in an abelian category.
A condition on a linear category over a field with finite-length objects and scalar simple-object endomorphisms.
In a Schur finite-length category, the endomorphism algebra of a simple object is equivalent to the base field.
The endomorphism space of a simple object is finite-dimensional in a Schur finite-length category.
Every morphism space in a Schur finite-length category is finite-dimensional.
Every object in a Schur finite-length category has finite length.
The maps obtained by left composition from a short exact complex form an exact pair.
The maps obtained by right composition from a short exact complex form an exact pair.
Finite-length source objects have finite-dimensional morphism spaces under the stated simple-object hypotheses.
Morphisms between simple objects are finite-dimensional when simple endomorphisms are finite-dimensional.
Morphisms from a simple object to a finite-length object are finite-dimensional under the stated hypothesis.
An exact sequence with finite-dimensional endpoints has a finite-dimensional middle space.
